content: 1. The Bangkok Tenofovir Study was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial conducted in Bangkok, Thailand, to evaluate the efficacy of antiretroviral prophylaxis for HIV prevention among injecting drug users. (Lancet, 2013; 381:2083–90) 2. Grant RM and colleagues conducted a study on pre-exposure chemoprophylaxis for HIV prevention in men who have sex with men, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2010 (363:2587–99). 3. Marrazzo JM et al. investigated tenofovir-based pre-exposure prophylaxis for HIV prevention among African women, with findings published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2015 (372:509–18). 4. Peterson L and colleagues conducted a phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial to assess the use of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate for HIV prevention in women, published in PLoS Clinical Trials in 2007 (2:e27). 5. Thigpen MC et al. studied antiretroviral pre-exposure prophylaxis for heterosexual HIV transmission in Botswana, with results published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2012 (367:423–34). 6. Van Damme L and colleagues evaluated pre-exposure prophylaxis for HIV prevention among African women, with their findings published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2012 (367:411–22). 7. McCormack S and Dunn D presented the results of the PROUD Study, a pragmatic open-label randomized trial of pre-exposure prophylaxis, at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections in Seattle, WA, USA, in February 2015. 8. Grohskopf LA et al. conducted a randomized trial to assess the clinical safety of daily oral tenofovir disoproxil fumarate among HIV-uninfected men who have sex with men in the United States, published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2013 (64:79–86). 9. The World Health Organization provided guidance on oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for serodiscordant couples, men, and transgender women at high risk of HIV, emphasizing its use in demonstration projects (accessed August 25, 2015). 10. Consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for key populations were published by the World Health Organization (accessed August 25, 2015). 11. Marrazzo JM et al. outlined recommendations for HIV prevention in clinical care settings in 2014, as part of the International Antiviral Society–USA Panel, published in JAMA (312:390–409). 12. Fonner G, Grant R, and Baggaley R conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the effectiveness, safety, and sexual and reproductive health outcomes of oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for all populations (unpublished). 13. Hoagland B et al. presented findings on PrEP uptake and associated factors among men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender women (TGW) in the PrEP Brasil demonstration project at the IAS 2015 conference in Vancouver, Canada. 14. Martin M et al. analyzed renal function among participants in the Bangkok Tenofovir Study conducted in Thailand from 2005 to 2012, with results published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2014 (59:716–24). 15. Solomon MM et al. examined changes in renal function associated with oral emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate use for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis, published in AIDS in 2014 (28:851–9). 16. Liu AY et al. studied bone mineral density in HIV-negative men participating in a tenofovir pre-exposure prophylaxis randomized clinical trial in San Francisco, published in PLoS One in 2011 (6:e23688). 17. Van de Vijver DA, Nichols BE, and Abbas UL modeled the limited impact of pre-exposure prophylaxis on HIV-1 drug resistance in sub-Saharan Africa, published in AIDS in 2013 (27:2943–51). 18. Marcus JL et al. found no evidence of sexual risk compensation in the iPrEx trial of daily oral HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis, published in PLoS One in 2013 (8:e81997). 19. Guest G et al. reported changes in sexual risk behavior among participants in a PrEP HIV prevention trial, published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2008 (35:1002–8). 20. Gomez GB et al. conducted a systematic review of cost-effectiveness modeling studies on the cost and impact of scaling up pre-exposure prophylaxis for HIV prevention, published in PLoS Medicine in 2013 (10:e1001401). 21. Hoagland B et al. presented data on PrEP uptake and associated factors among MSM and TGW in the PrEP Brasil demonstration project at the IAS 2015 conference in Vancouver, Canada. 22. Médecins Sans Frontières published the 17th edition of Untangling the Web of Antiretroviral Price Reductions in 2014. 23. Bekker LG et al. compared daily and non-daily PrEP dosing in African women as part of the HPTN 067/ADAPT Cape Town study, presented at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections in Seattle, WA, USA, in February 2015. 24. Henderson FL et al. analyzed characteristics and oral PrEP adherence in the TDF2 open-label extension in Botswana, presented at the IAS 2015 conference in Vancouver, Canada. 25. Mannheimer S et al. compared daily and intermittent PrEP dosing for HIV prevention among MSM and TGW in New York City as part of the HPTN 067/ADAPT study, presented at the IAS 2015 conference in Vancouver, Canada. 26. Holtz TH et al. compared daily and non-daily PrEP dosing among Thai MSM in Bangkok, Thailand, as part of the HPTN 067/ADAPT study, presented at the IAS 2015 conference in Vancouver, Canada. 27. Liu A et al. examined adherence, sexual behavior, and HIV/STI incidence among MSM and TGW in the US PrEP demonstration project, presented at the IAS 2015 conference in Vancouver, Canada. 28. Hosek S et al. conducted a PrEP demonstration project and safety study for young MSM in the United States (ATN 110), presented at the IAS 2015 conference in Vancouver, Canada. 29. Machtinger EL et al. discussed the promise of trauma-informed primary care in transitioning from treatment to healing, published in Women's Health Issues in 2015 (25:193–7). 30. Cottrell ML et al. developed a novel PK-PD model to predict effective Truvada® PrEP dosing strategies, incorporating tissue-active metabolites and endogenous nucleotides, presented at the R4P conference in Cape Town, South Africa, in October 2014. 31. Ford N, Mayer KH, and the WHO Postexposure Prophylaxis Guideline Development Group published WHO guidelines on postexposure prophylaxis for HIV, emphasizing a public health approach, in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2015 (60 Suppl. 3:S161–4). 32. Ehrhardt S et al. reviewed evidence on breastfeeding while taking lamivudine or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2015 (60:275–9). 33. WHO published a technical brief on the surveillance of antiretroviral drug toxicity within antiretroviral treatment programs (accessed August 25, 2015). 34. WHO released consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services in 2015, accessible online (accessed August 25, 2015). 35. WHO published consolidated strategic information guidelines for HIV in the health sector, including recommendations on when to start antiretroviral therapy and pre-exposure prophylaxis for HIV. 36. The Clinical Guideline Development Group declared no conflicts of interest during their June 2015 meeting, with management plans in place for any potential conflicts.
